title: reduce GPU memory and workspace: arena tuning, activation checkpointing, scratch buffers
author: Priya Raman
description:
Motivation: reduce per-GPU peak memory and workspace requirements for large-model inference workloads so we can host longer context models with the same instance sizes and improve packing efficiency for continuous batching. This PR combines three coordinated changes: 1) conservative activation checkpointing for attention and FFN blocks to trade a small amount of CPU recompute for large activation savings, 2) heap/arena tuning to reduce fragmentation and per-request temporary workspace allocations, and 3) a scratch buffer pool and reuse policy to avoid repeated malloc/free during token generation. The change set also includes small kernel-level adjustments and KV cache layout tweaks to further reduce peak footprint when K-V cache is populated.

What changed (summary):
- activation checkpointing: introduce optional lightweight checkpointing for attention/FFN kernels with heuristics driven by model size and sequence length. Default off for small models, enabled automatically for models > 7B with sequence lengths > 2k.
- arena tuning: reduce default arena block size, add a fast-path for small fixed-size allocations, and expose an env var REDWOOD_GPU_ARENA_MAX_BIN to tune in customers.
- scratch buffer pool: implement a thread-local pool of reusable scratch buffers with size classes aligned to typical kernel workspace needs; avoids repeated cudaMalloc/cudaFree during generation.
- KV cache layout: compact K-V storage for fp16/quantized backends to remove padding in the common-case sequence distribution.
- scheduler tweaks: the continuous batcher now prefers packing requests that will benefit from the scratch buffer reuse and reduced arena overhead; additional backpressure metrics exposed for autoscaler.
- tests and perf harness: add unit tests and a perf microbenchmark that reproduces memory improvements for a 13B model at 4k context.

Checklist:
- [x] design doc and perf plan linked in ENG-3241
- [x] unit and integration tests updated/added
- [x] perf runs demonstrating ~18-28% peak GPU memory reduction on 13B/30B workloads in our lab
- [x] env var documented for ops teams
- [x] staged rollout plan (canary then fleet)

Backward compatibility and safe rollout notes: changes are opt-in via model heuristics and a per-deployment config flag. Default for previously pinned models remains unchanged. Arena tuning can be overridden by REDWOOD_GPU_ARENA_MAX_BIN and the checkpointing toggle.

Release notes: see release_notes field.

release_notes:
- Reduced peak GPU memory for long-context inference by 18-28% (13B/30B workloads) via activation checkpointing, arena tuning, and scratch buffer reuse.
- New env var REDWOOD_GPU_ARENA_MAX_BIN to control arena behavior.
- Per-model flag to opt models into checkpointing heuristics.
